title: Etale topos point arrows are geometric lifts into the target strict localization
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_t\to S$ and $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_s\to S$ be geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point], with $\Omega_t,\Omega_s$ algebraically closed. Let $S_{(\bar s)}$ be the inverse limit of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with structural morphism $\rho:S_{(\bar s)}\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Regard the geometric points as points of the small etale topos [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; arrows are $2$-morphisms defined on direct images [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and their inverse-image mates act on set-valued geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. There is a canonical bijection
$$\Theta:\{a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_t\to S_{(\bar s)}\mid \rho a=\bar t\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(\bar t,\bar s).$$
For a lift $a$, the mate of $\Theta(a)$ sends a represented germ $[U,\bar u,z]$ at $\bar s$ to $[U,c_{U,\bar u}a,z]$ at $\bar t$, where $c_{U,\bar u}:S_{(\bar s)}\to U$ is the canonical neighbourhood projection (using affine refinements if $U$ is not affine). For every field automorphism $\tau$ of $\Omega_t$ satisfying $\bar t\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau=\bar t$, changing geometric lifts by $\bar v\mapsto\bar v\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau$ defines an automorphism $r_\tau$ of the point $\bar t$, and
$$\Theta(a\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau)=\Theta(a)\circ r_\tau.$$
No normality, Noetherian, finite-type, support-specialization, or algebraicity-of-$\Omega_t$ hypothesis is required.
